thread:
raj: Heads-up — we had 6 alerts across two clusters in the last hour for dcgm_exporter ECC spikes on multiple cards. Looks like noisy bursts after the kernel update on 03/17.

olivia: Saw those. Most of them are short lived (10-40s) and happen on different GPUs of the same node. Alerts are drowning out real Xid failures.

sam: Can you paste the Alertmanager payload? wondering if alerts are per-node or per-card.

raj: payload snippets: 
- alertname: GPU_ECC_ERROR
  node: gpu-node-12
  gpu_index: "1"
  value: 4
  startedAt: 2026-03-17T18:03:12Z

olivia: These are per-gpu (dcgm_gpu_ecc_counts_total{gpu_index, instance}). Our current Prom rule fires when increase(dcgm_gpu_ecc_counts_total[5m]) > 0 with for: 0m which is too sensitive.

maria: Agreed. Two immediate levers: 1) record a smoothed metric (rate or rolling-sum) and alert on that, 2) make rule local to a node and coalesce alerts by gpu_index label so Alertmanager groups them.

raj: Proposed recording rule to reduce noise: 
```
- record: infra:gpu_ecc:sum5m
  expr: increase(dcgm_gpu_ecc_counts_total[5m])
```
Then alert using something like: 
```
- alert: GPU_ECC_PersistentSpike
  expr: infra:gpu_ecc:sum5m > 3
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Persistent ECC spikes on {{ $labels.instance }} gpu {{ $labels.gpu_index }}"
```
That hits when multiple spikes accumulate over a window instead of firing on single blips.

nate: Also consider per-gpu histograms for distribution of spikes so we can filter post-kernel transient behavior. Might be overkill for now.

sam: We should also add node-local recording rules in the agent's scrape target so we don't aggregate across nodes. Right now some rules lose gpu_index label after recording and group across nodes which is confusing.

olivia: +1. I'll submit a PR for two changes: (A) a recording rule infra:gpu_ecc:rate5m with label_keep on instance,gpu_index and (B) change the alert to use >3 and for: 10m. I'll include grouping by (instance, gpu_index) in alertmanager.

raj: Another idea — add a rolling-unixtime counter to detect 'burstiness' pattern: alert when count spikes repeatedly across 3 consecutive 5m windows. Example PromQL: 
```
(sum_over_time(increase(dcgm_gpu_ecc_counts_total[5m])[15m:5m]) > 6)
```
This is a bit gnarly but it reduces single-window noise.

maria: Keep it understandable for oncall. Prefer the simpler recording + for:10m approach and update runbook. We'll iterate if noise persists.

infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0417-08 (auto) — noisy GPU ECC alerts on cluster-us-west2. Assigned to eng-infra oncall.

sam: Action plan: 
1) olivia PR for recording + alert changes (staging first) — target: today EOD.
2) deploy to staging alerting stack, run synthetic spike test script (attach below).
3) if staging passes, roll to prod with 30m canary (apply to 10% of nodes via prometheus relabeling).
4) update runbook and Alertmanager grouping/route to mute transient severity.

olivia: test script (simple): 
```
# simulate ecc counter bump on gpu 0 of node-12
curl -XPOST http://staging-metrics-proxy/gpu-bump -d '{"node":"gpu-node-12","gpu_index":0,"delta":5}'
```
I'll add a small harness that calls it 3x in 2 minutes to simulate noisy bursts.

raj: Drain/replace threshold: ops consensus was >50 persistent ECCs over 24h or repeated Xid errors. For now we won't auto-drain on these alerts; just page after triage. Update runbook to show kubectl drain command: 
```
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
```
And annotate node with gpu-failed label: 
```
kubectl label node <node> gpu-failed=true --overwrite
```

maria: Good. Also coordinate with kernel team: open ticket referencing kernel 5.15.82-rc that rolled 03/17. Need to correlate node reboot times with spike start times.

nate: Will add Grafana panel for 'spike frequency over time' per gpu_index and an alert heatmap. That should help spot bad cards vs systemic kernel regressions.

olivia: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-monitoring/pull/847 — includes recording rule + updated alert + test harness. Pushed to staging alerting namespace.

raj: Thanks. I'll monitor Alertmanager and mute noisy routes if we see repeats. If the staging run produces false negatives we revert to narrower for window.

maria: Update runbook and close INC when we confirm baseline noise reduced. Assign follow-ups: @nate add dashboard, @sam add drain threshold note, @raj coordinate kernel ticket.

sam: ack, will add runbook snippets and include exact PromQL examples.

olivia: leaving logs of the staging test here after 10m: 
```
[2026-03-17T20:12:00Z] bump gpu-node-12:0 +5
[2026-03-17T20:13:10Z] bump gpu-node-12:0 +3
[2026-03-17T20:14:55Z] bump gpu-node-12:0 +2
Alert: no page fired (expected) — alert fired only when sum>3 over 10m window after second bump.
```

raj: Perfect. Closing loop — we'll let this bake overnight and evaluate tomorrow morning (1798432450). :thumbsup:
